touches.text: TICKET (Abstract class - not a device, but a first class object; abstract)

The abstract ticket owns what every kind shares: its birth (cast) and its three parts, each with one job: the plan (only what a builder builds from), the metadata and state (what gates and doors read and write as it moves), and the history (the append-only log). WHY: one job per part reduces confusion; a builder reads the plan and nothing else (Akien, 2026-10-29 and 2026-11-02).
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
Machine: the operator inbox (today the operator_inbox tool, 19.17) builds the to-do list from live state, storing nothing.

Owns the inspectors and gates (draft, moving from standalone): build_inspector, plan_inspector, ticket_inspector, corrosion, exemptions, rehearsal, determinism, import_sieve, and the tester (11; Q#33, Akien 2026-10-29). (Not diagnostic_inspector: it is base's, 17.3.) The code pipeline's inspectors and gates move to CodeMother; any that are not about code (if such existed) would not. (Q#31, Akien 2026-10-27)
gate: the == compare, in one place. A gate opens when every expected equals its actual. No oracle, ever.
operator_inbox: builds the operator's to-do list from live state. → Operator's machine (8.2.7)
question: the open-question door: a decision only you can make, bound to its ticket, answered in your words. → Ticket (3.3.5)? Operator?

conflicts.text: The inspectors are not assumed correct; they are examined when they refuse. A failure is not automatically "it broke, change it". After a gate refuses, an LLM sets the refusing sieve's intention and why beside the ticket's intention and why and asks: is this sieve the best we can do right now? If yes, the ticket changes. If no, the sieve is fixed. Either way the system improves, constantly. WHY: questions about a part are answered by its intention and why against the new thing's intention and why, so a disagreement becomes an update to an intention or to its implementation plan, never a conversation about procedure (Akien, 2026-11-02). The sieves stay deterministic and never weigh a why; the LLM check comes only after a failure. It is never a lock pick because it has no third outcome: the ticket changes, or the sieve is fixed through its own ticket and proof. Nothing passes a ticket over a red; testing a sieve is what the ticket that fixes it does. (Q#62, Akien 2026-11-02.)
conflicts.ticket_says: intention and why are moved from the ticket to berths pointed to by owning_intention; gates access them via that address, not as direct ticket properties
conflicts.why: Outline assumes 'the ticket's intention and why' are directly accessible properties when gates examine failures. Ticket removes these fields from the ticket object entirely, storing them in external berths instead. Gates can no longer access them as described — they must dereference owning_intention first.
